content: The global incidence and prevalence of medulloblastoma are approximately 1 per 100,000 individuals. Medulloblastoma is a rare disease that predominantly affects children. The incidence of medulloblastoma decreases with age, with the median age at diagnosis being 5 years. Males are more frequently affected by medulloblastoma compared to females, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 2:1. Medulloblastomas affect just under 2 individuals per million per year and are 10 times more common in children than in adults. Among newly diagnosed cases, 5% occur in adults. In adults, medulloblastoma is exceedingly rare, accounting for fewer than 2% of central nervous system malignancies. The incidence of childhood medulloblastoma is higher in males (62%) than in females (38%), a gender disparity that is not observed in adult cases. Medulloblastoma and other primitive neuroectodermal tumors (PNETs) are more prevalent in younger children compared to older children. Only 7% of cases occur in individuals aged 15 to 19 years.
